summary.text: A nebula is a distinct luminescent part of the interstellar medium, made of ionized, neutral or molecular hydrogen and cosmic dust.
Many nebulae are star-forming regions, where gas and dust clump into denser regions that attract more matter and eventually become dense enough to form stars.
Most nebulae are vast, yet far less dense than any vacuum made on Earth, so a nebular cloud the size of Earth would hold only a few kilograms.

items.prompt: A 19th-century catalogue lists the Andromeda Galaxy among cloud-like objects. What explains that?

options.label: It was thought to be a star cluster hidden in dust
Galaxies were then known to be small gas clouds
The term covered any diffuse object, galaxies included
The galaxy's light was bent by Earth's thick air layer

items.explain: The term nebula originally described any diffused astronomical object, including galaxies beyond the Milky Way, until the early 20th century.

items.prompt: A nebula that you can see from Earth is approached by a spacecraft. What would the crew notice about it?

options.label: It would look larger, but no brighter
It would look both larger and brighter
It would look smaller and dimmer
It would look the same size but much brighter

items.explain: A nebula visible from Earth would appear larger, but no brighter, from close by.

items.prompt: A lab builds the best vacuum it can on Earth. How does a typical nebula compare with it?

options.label: About as empty as the best Earth vacuum
Thousands of times denser than that vacuum
As dense as the air in a room
Far less dense than the best Earth vacuum

items.explain: Although denser than the space around them, most nebulae are far less dense than any vacuum created on Earth.

items.prompt: Gas and dust in a nebula are clumping into denser patches. What can happen as those patches grow?

options.label: They scatter back out into empty space
They attract more matter and can become dense enough to form stars
They freeze into a solid shell
They turn into a galaxy beyond the Milky Way

items.explain: The clumps attract further matter and eventually become dense enough to form stars.

items.prompt: Many nebulae glow rather than staying dark. What makes a lot of them visible?

options.label: Fusion burning in the nebula's own gas
Radio waves from the galaxy's center lighting the gas
Fluorescence caused by hot stars embedded in them
Heat left behind by a black hole inside

items.explain: Many nebulae are visible due to fluorescence caused by embedded hot stars.

items.prompt: In 1912 Vesto Slipher found that the spectrum of the nebula around the star Merope matched the Pleiades open cluster. What did that show?

options.label: The nebula makes its own light by fusion
The nebula glows by a gas's own emission
The nebula is really a galaxy
The nebula shines by reflecting light from nearby stars

items.explain: Because its spectrum matched that of the cluster's stars, the nebula radiates by reflected star light.
